title: DOE RM1: Experimental Results — Hill et al.
reviewed_sections: report printed pp.3-10 experimental setup, processing and uncertainty
report printed pp.12-13 turbine performance and blockage limits
report printed p.20 Appendix A 32 tabulated right/left rotor operating points
supported_claims: The report documents RM1 experimental methodology and reported combined power-coefficient measurement uncertainty of approximately 3.9%.
Appendix A permits reproducing 16 Cp-vs-TSR performance points per rotor and checking nominal torque-rotation mechanical power, but no directly measured turbine thrust
Right-rotor tabulated Cp peak 0.477; left rotor max 0.412 while report text gives approximate left Cp peak 0.43
limitations: Selected experimental sections and Appendix A reviewed; NOT a full-report deep review, no raw torque and velocity series or independently validated model.
2014 introduction mistakenly labels RM1 as RM2; do not propagate.
TSR and Cp from printed table have limited precision and source Cp does not equal a simple ratio of printed mean values.
Thrust and Ct are n/a in Appendix A; RM1 does not demonstrate fatigue-life benefit.
access_status: Public Sandia PDF with readable performance table and graphical appendix; PDF p.20 screenshot inspected.

title: Viehman et al. Integrated Hydroacoustic Approaches to Predict Fish Interactions with In-stream Tidal Turbines (FORCE/OERA final report)
reviewed_sections: PDF pp.5-8 (deployment and instrument methods, including sec.3.2.2)
PDF pp.15-16 (sec.3.4.1 ADCP currents quality treatment and declination correction)
supported_claims: FAST3 platform included an upward-looking Nortek Signature 500 ADCP in March-May 2018; five-minute bursts every 15 minutes, 2-Hz burst rate.
Reported treatment of ADCP data includes estimating water surface from echo amplitude and excluding top 10% of the column for sidelobes during project analyses.
North/east component rotation in the published processed ERDDAP product needs separate lineage confirmation before any additional direction adjustment.
limitations: The report does not provide explicit instrument serial-specific head height above seafloor for public ERDDAP product, beam correlation/percent-good for individual cell records or a direct zero-fill convention.
Report describes original SDU processing; cannot conclude published ERDDAP ENU has or has not applied declination without transformation code.
Automated page images from primary report were access-blocked; reviewed text extraction and source identification, not visually verified figure geometry.
access_status: Public PDF text and primary metadata accessible; images intermittently 403; reviewed stated sections only.

title: Viehman, Hasselman, Douglas & Boucher (2022): The Ups and Downs of Using Active Acoustic Technologies to Study Fish at Tidal Energy Sites
reviewed_sections: 2.1 Data Collection, FAST3 installation and Nortek ADCP geometry
2.2.2 ADCP Data, tilt, declination and upper 10% acoustic sidelobe exclusion
supported_claims: March-May 2018 FAST3 Nortek Signature 500 face 0.7 m above seafloor, 1-m blanking distance and 1-m cells; first cell center 2 m from transducer face, 2-Hz burst sampling for 5 min per 15 minutes.
Study processed native ADCP tilt/declination and excluded top 10% water column from scientific current averages due to sidelobes.
limitations: The paper reports its own experimental processing; public CIOOS ERDDAP cell_range begins 1.5m, not a confirmed geometric match to first cell centre 2m, so absolute bin heights cannot be asserted.
No per-vector beam-quality fields or unique zero-fill convention established for the processed ERDDAP product; publication does not certify every public data cell.
Ecological fish acoustics focus, not certified turbine resource, loading or site viability.
access_status: Public peer-reviewed original full-text HTML sections directly examined.

title: Naberezhnykh et al. (2023), How Applicable Are Turbulence Assumptions Used in the Tidal Energy Industry?
reviewed_sections: Abstract: measured turbulence models and site variability
Table 1: EMEC and FORCE 2018/2022 ADCP study campaigns
Discussion and conclusions on shear, spectra and turbulence assumptions
Data Availability Statement: third-party restricted source measurements
supported_claims: The study compared field turbulence with commonly assumed spectral/shear/coherence representations at EMEC and FORCE and reports notable site/depth deviations.
Turbulence spectra and shear assumptions can materially affect simulated turbine loads; site-specific measurement is required for robust loads comparison.

2022 and other FORCE campaigns listed are NOT the same 2018 100258 processed publication and cannot substitute QC for it.
Paper does not quantify our turbine structural life, test-site turbine resource, or supplier accessibility.

title: UNH RM2 tow-tank processed performance curves at 0.4–1.2 m/s — paired published speed-series evidence
reviewed_sections: README Test matrix sections: five nominal tow speeds and second (-b) performance curves
Mean TSR, mean Cp, mean Cd and exp_unc_* processed columns for nominal source runs 10 and 12; Cp maximum from each source series
supported_claims: Ten processed source series comprise first/second performance sweeps at each of five nominal freshwater towing speeds 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0 and 1.2 m/s.
Across the ten published point-estimate comparisons, nominal TSR 2.9 has lower reported mean Cp and mean Cd than nominal TSR 3.1, but relative Cp difference varies strongly with tow speed.
Original 1m/s ~1.85% Cp and ~5.51% mean Cd difference does not generalize as a fixed low-energy-cost drag derating across speeds.
limitations: Only processed upstream means and source uncertainty columns reviewed; no raw synchronized strain/phase/torque/source uncertainty covariance or statistically powered independent trials.
Second sweeps are repeat performance curves of one scaled rotor, NOT ten independent turbines or evidence of full-scale reliability.
Tank blockage and Reynolds dependence, hydrodynamic shear and turbulence remain uncorrected/not independently validated here.
The comparison uses fixed nominal TSR 2.9 vs 3.1, not the observed maximum Cp in all series; no optimized controller, net electrical, physical fatigue, site hydrodynamics, ecological or LCOE claims.
Do not extrapolate to axial RM1 or nonrotating foil across incompatible power denominators.
access_status: Public CC BY 4.0 upstream processed CSVs and README, 10 exact source Git blob SHAs pinned in reduced fixture
